reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds a shared isHoliday, and the new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, but the daily-skip rule is not put behind any shared function, so each consumer rebuilds it.

duplication.why: The 'daily with weekend handling skips non-business days, otherwise adjust' logic (isDailyWithSkippedWeekends / isNonBusinessDay / filter / conditional getDateWithSkippedWeekend) is written three times: getNextDate in shared/schedules.ts, and getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in schedules/app.ts.

placement.why: Holiday matching and weekend moving are rightly in shared/schedules.ts, but the occurrence-level skip/adjust rule is spread into server handlers instead of living next to it.

scope.why: The changes serve the four steps; the RecurConfig type and schedule-template holiday pass-through are in scope.

maintainability.why: Three slightly different copies (one lowercases frequency, others do not; ad-hoc take multipliers like count * (holidays.length + 2) and holidays.length + 7) and schedule-template still moves daily weekend dates rather than skipping them, so the rule already diverges.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly and never applies the daily-skip rule; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement it instead of sharing getNextDate's logic.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip predicate is renamed per copy (skipsDailyWeekend/skipsDailyNonBusinessDay in getNextDate vs isDailyWithSkippedWeekends/isNonBusinessDay in schedules/app.ts) and reshaped (start-jumping loop vs filter over over-fetched occurrences).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; the daily special case is kept outside it as conditional branches in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and schedule-template.ts bypasses the daily rule entirely (getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template counted as bypassing/re-implementing).
